text: `top` (Shift+P to sort by %CPU) shows `batch-report-job` and `telemetry-agent` both burning CPU, roughly evenly. The `PR`/`NI` columns are worth a look -- `NI` is the nice value each process is running at.

Get precise: `ps -o pid,ni,pcpu,cmd -p $(cat /var/run/batch-report-job.pid),$(cat /var/run/telemetry-agent.pid)`. Both show `NI` 0 -- same priority class, so on a CPU-constrained box they're roughly splitting it 50/50 no matter which one matters more.

The box's runbook says `telemetry-agent` must always run deprioritized so it doesn't compete evenly with real work like `batch-report-job`. Its niceness is config-driven: `/etc/telemetry-agent/telemetry-agent.conf` sets `NICE_LEVEL=0` -- reset to the default in a recent redeploy instead of whatever higher (lower-priority) value it's supposed to be.

Renice it immediately, live, no restart needed: `sudo renice 15 -p $(cat /var/run/telemetry-agent.pid)`. Note the direction -- you can only *raise* another process's niceness (deprioritize it) without special privileges the container doesn't grant here; you can't lower one back down once raised, so there's no way to accidentally fix this by reniceing the wrong process further down. For a durable fix that survives a restart, also correct the config: `sudo sed -i 's/NICE_LEVEL=0/NICE_LEVEL=15/' /etc/telemetry-agent/telemetry-agent.conf` (takes effect next time `svc-ctl restart` runs it).
